# Libraries

```{r}
# load libraries
library(FLCore)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggrepel)
library(flextable)

library(GGally)
library(ggcorrplot)
library(car)
library(MASS)

library(mgcv)
library(gratia)
library(brms)

library(readxl)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 16))
```

# Data preparation

```{r}
# load object from WGHANSA 2022
load(file.path("..","data","aneq.stk.RData")) # aneq.stk

# remove 2023

aneq.stk <- window(aneq.stk, end=2022)

# recruitment (1st January)
# change units

rec <- rec(aneq.stk)
rec <- rec*1e-6
units(rec) <- "1e9"

# ssb (from FLBiols because it is the same as used in FLBEIA)

aneq.biol <- as(aneq.stk, "FLBiol")
ssb <- ssb(aneq.biol)
# equivalently, (i.e. without fishing mortality)
# quantSums(stock.n(aneq.stk)*exp(-m(aneq.stk)*m.spwn(aneq.stk))*stock.wt(aneq.stk)*mat(aneq.stk))
ssb <- ssb/1000
units(ssb) <- "1000 t"

# create data frame

df <- data.frame(year=as.numeric(dimnames(aneq.stk)$year), 
                 rec=as.numeric(rec), 
                 ssb=as.numeric(ssb))

# create log variables

df <- df %>% 
  mutate(logr=log(rec),
         logssb=log(ssb),
         rat=rec/ssb, 
         lograt=log(rat))

dat <- read.csv(file.path("..","data","env_data.csv"), sep=",")

df <- left_join(df, dat)
df <- subset(df, select=-c(date)) # remove the date column (which is a character)
names(df)
```

# Basic Ricker fitted as lm

```{r}
# all years:
m0.2022 <- lm(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb, data=df)
coef(m0.2022)

# given that there are no env data in 2022, the reference model is until 2021
m0 <- lm(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb, data=subset(df, year<2022)) 
# equivalently: 
# m0bis <- lm(lograt ~ ssb, data=df)

coef(m0)
summary(m0)
anova(m0)
confint(m0, level=0.95)

plot(m0)

df$res <- residuals(m0.2022) # we include the residuals in df
 
```

# Exploratory analysis 1987-2021

Cross-correlation analysis: 

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}
mat <- cor(df, use="complete.obs", method="pearson") 
p.mat <- cor_pmat(df)
ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", p.mat = p.mat, legend.title="Pearson corr")

mat <- cor(df, use="complete.obs", method="spearman") 
p.mat <- cor_pmat(df, method="spearman")
ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", p.mat = p.mat, legend.title="Spearman corr")

```

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}

envsel <- c("AMO.mean","AMO.q1",
         "EA.mean","EA.max","EA.s2",
         "NAO.mean","NAO.sd",
         "TURB.mean","TURB.q3",
         "UI","WMLD")
vsel <- c("logr","logssb","ssb","lograt","res",
         envsel)

tmp <- subset(df, select=vsel)

mat <- cor(tmp, use="complete.obs") 
p.mat <- cor_pmat(tmp)
ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", p.mat = p.mat, legend.title="Pearson corr")

mat <- cor(tmp, use="complete.obs", method="spearman") 
p.mat <- cor_pmat(tmp, method="spearman")
ggcorrplot(mat, type = "lower", p.mat = p.mat, legend.title="Spearman Corr")

```

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}
ggpairs(subset(df, select=vsel)) 
```

Time series of selected explanatory variables: 

```{r, fig.width=15, fig.height=15}
tmp <- pivot_longer(df, cols=-year)
tmp <- subset(tmp, name %in% vsel)
p <- ggplot(tmp, aes(year, value, group=name))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_smooth(stat="smooth", col=2, fill=2, alpha=0.3)+ 
  facet_wrap(~ factor(name, levels=vsel), scales="free")+ # to reorder the levels in the plot
  xlab("")+
  ylab("")
p

```

VIF analysis:

```{r}
m.all <- lm(as.formula(paste("logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb +", paste(envsel,collapse="+"))), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(m.all)
anova(m.all)
out.vif <- vif(m.all) # function in the car library

p <- ggplot(data.frame(vif=out.vif, name=names(out.vif)), aes(name, vif))+
  geom_bar(stat="identity", col="blue", fill="blue")+
  geom_hline(yintercept=5, lty=2, lwd=1)+
  coord_flip()
p

#The value for VIF starts at 1 and has no upper limit. A general rule of thumb for interpreting VIFs is as follows:

#A value of 1 indicates there is no correlation between a given predictor variable and any other predictor variables in the model.
#A value between 1 and 5 indicates moderate correlation between a given predictor variable and other predictor variables in the model, but this is often not severe enough to require attention.
#A value greater than 5 indicates potentially severe correlation between a given predictor variable and other predictor variables in the model. In this case, the coefficient estimates and p-values in the regression output are likely unreliable.
```

These are the most plausible models, according to the level of significance of the variables:  

```{r}
m1 <- lm(as.formula(paste("logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb +", paste(c("UI","TURB.q3","EA.s2"),collapse="+"))), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(m1)

m2 <- lm(as.formula(paste("logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb +", paste(c("UI","TURB.q3"),collapse="+"))), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(m2)

m3 <- lm(as.formula(paste("logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb +", paste(c("UI"),collapse="+"))), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(m3)

anova(m0, m3, m2, m1)
AIC(m0, m3, m2, m1)
BIC(m0, m3, m2, m1)
```

# Ricker with environmental variables (linear)

Stepwise backward selection:

```{r}
# we remove AMO.mean because the last year is complete, so the last year value is not correct
# we remove WMLD because it has 2 NA's

envsel <- c("AMO.q1", 
         "EA.mean","EA.max","EA.s2",
         "NAO.mean","NAO.sd",
         "TURB.mean","TURB.q3",
         "UI")
```

```{r}
modback <- stepAIC(m.all, trace=TRUE, direction="backward")
modback$anova
summary(modback)


modforw <- stepAIC(m0, trace=TRUE, direction="forward", scope=as.formula(paste("logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb +", paste(envsel,collapse="+"))))
modforw$anova
summary(modforw)

modboth <- stepAIC(m0, trace=TRUE, direction="both", scope=as.formula(paste("logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb +", paste(envsel,collapse="+"))))
modboth$anova
summary(modboth)

```

# Ricker with environmental variables (smooths)

```{r}
mm01 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(AMO.q1), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm02 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(EA.mean), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm03 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(EA.s2), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm04 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(NAO.mean), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm05 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(TURB.mean), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm06 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(TURB.q3), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm07 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(UI), data=subset(df, year<2022))
mm08 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(WMLD), data=subset(df, year<2022))

summary(mm01)
summary(mm02)
summary(mm03)
summary(mm04)
summary(mm05)
summary(mm06)
summary(mm07)
summary(mm08)

unlist(lapply(list(mm01, mm02, mm03, mm04, mm05, mm06, mm07, mm08), function(x) x$gcv.ubre))
unlist(lapply(list(mm01, mm02, mm03, mm04, mm05, mm06, mm07, mm08), AIC))

mm09 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(UI) + s(TURB.q3), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(mm09)
gam.check(mm09)
draw(mm09) # using gratia
draw(mm09, residuals=T) # using gratia
appraise(mm09) # using gratia
unlist(lapply(list(mm06, mm07, mm09), function(x) x$gcv.ubre))
unlist(lapply(list(mm06, mm07, mm09), AIC))

mm10 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + s(TURB.q3), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(mm10)
gam.check(mm10)
plot(mm10)
draw(mm10) # using gratia
draw(mm10, residuals=T) # using gratia
appraise(mm10) # using gratia

mm0 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb , data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(mm0)


mm10b <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + s(TURB.q3), data=subset(df, year<2022), method="REML")
summary(mm10b)
gam.check(mm10b)
plot(mm10b)

anova(mm06, mm09, test="F")
anova(mm07, mm09, test="F")

tmp0 <- predict(m0, newdata=df, type="response", se.fit=T)
tmp1 <- predict(mm10, newdata=df, type="response", se.fit=T)
pred.dat <- data.frame(year=df$year, rec=df$rec, ssb=df$ssb,
                       fit0=tmp0$fit, se.fit0=tmp0$se.fit, 
                       fit1=tmp1$fit, se.fit1=tmp1$se.fit)
p <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(year, log(rec)))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_line(aes(year, fit1), col=2)+
  geom_point(aes(year, fit1), col=2, pch=1)+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=fit1-se.fit1, ymax=fit1+se.fit1), col=2, fill=2, alpha=0.5)+
  geom_line(aes(year, fit0), col=4)+
  geom_point(aes(year, fit0), col=4, pch=1)+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=fit0-se.fit0, ymax=fit0+se.fit0), col=4, fill=4, alpha=0.5)+
  xlab("")+
  ylab("log(rec)")
print(p)

p <- ggplot(pred.dat)+
  geom_point(aes(year, y=log(rec)-fit1), col=2)+
  geom_line(aes(year, y=log(rec)-fit1), col=2)+
  geom_point(aes(year, y=log(rec)-fit0), col=4)+
  geom_line(aes(year, y=log(rec)-fit0), col=4)+
  ylab("Residuals")+
  xlab("")
print(p)


p <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(year, fit0))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=fit0-se.fit0, ymax=fit0+se.fit0), fill="grey", alpha=0.5)+
  geom_line(col=1)+
  geom_point(data=pred.dat, aes(x=year, y=log(rec)))+
  xlab("")+
  ylab("Log Recruits (age 0)")+
  expand_limits(y=0)
p

p <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(year, fit1))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=fit1-se.fit1, ymax=fit1+se.fit1), fill="grey", alpha=0.5)+
  geom_line(col=1)+
  geom_point(data=pred.dat, aes(x=year, y=log(rec)))+
  xlab("")+
  ylab("Log Recruits (age 0)")+
  expand_limits(y=0)
p


tmp0 <- predict(m0, newdata=data.frame(ssb=seq(0.1, 220, length=500), logssb=log(seq(0.1, 220, length=500))), type="response", se.fit=T)
pred.dat <- data.frame(ssb=seq(0.1, 220, length=500),
                       fit0=tmp0$fit, se.fit0=tmp0$se.fit)

p <- ggplot(pred.dat, aes(ssb, exp(fit0)))+
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin=exp(fit0-se.fit0), ymax=exp(fit0+se.fit0)), fill="grey", alpha=0.5)+
  geom_line(col=1)+
  geom_point(data=df, aes(x=ssb, y=rec))+
  xlab("SSB")+
  ylab("Recruits (age 0)")+
  expand_limits(y=0, x=0)
p

```

# approximate model by linear terms

```{r}
ss10 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + TURB.q3 + I(TURB.q3^2) + I(TURB.q3^3), data=subset(df, year<2022))
# equivalently: 
# ss10b <- glm(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + poly(TURB.q3, 3), data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(ss10)
gam.check(ss10)
plot(ss10, all.term=T, ask=F)
draw(ss10, parametric=T) # using gratia
draw(ss10, parametric=T, residuals=T) # using gratia
appraise(ss10) # using gratia

mm11 <- gam(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + TURB.q3, data=subset(df, year<2022))
summary(mm11)
gam.check(mm11)
plot(mm11, all.term=T, ask=F)
draw(mm11, parametric=T) # using gratia
draw(mm11, parametric=T, residuals=T) # using gratia
appraise(mm11) # using gratia

```

# Using brms

```{r, eval=F}
bb1 <- brm(bf(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + UI + TURB.q3),
          data = df, family = gaussian(), cores = 4, seed = 17,
          iter = 4000, warmup = 1000, thin = 10, refresh = 0,
          control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))

summary(bb1)



bb2 <- brm(bf(logr ~ offset(logssb) + ssb + s(UI) + s(TURB.q3)),
          data = df, family = gaussian(), cores = 4, seed = 17,
          iter = 4000, warmup = 1000, thin = 10, refresh = 0,
          control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99))

summary(bb2)
plot(marginal_smooths(bb2))
```
